sections.text: A String works as an error for small programs, but an enum describes exactly what went wrong and lets callers react to each case.
Implement Display to give each error a friendly message, so it can be printed with {}:
To let ? turn other errors into yours, implement From:
This lesson pulls together enums, match, impl and Result. If it feels like a lot, that's normal. Come back to it after a few more units.
In real projects, the thiserror crate generates Display and From for error enums, and anyhow gives applications a convenient catch-all error type.

exercise.prompt: Add a Display impl for ShopError so the program prints the friendly message. It should print: Error: out of stock

quiz.question: Why use an enum for errors instead of a String?
options: Callers can react to each kind of error

quiz.question: Which trait lets an error be printed with {}?
What does implementing From<ParseIntError> for your error let you do?
options: Use ? on parse results in your functions
